doc.title: Marty Sheller interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 9, 2022

title: Roseland union hall, pickup gigs and pay
summary: Musicians looking for work at Roseland, pickup gig pay of $25-30, and the union pension he missed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Thank you for that. That’s a terrific story. What was it like to, you must have been in the musician’s union eventually.
And if you’re looking for work you go down to the musician’s union hall and like hang?

Yes. Well I don’t know how it is now but because I live in Delaware, I’m out of that scene. But it used to be every Monday, Wednesday and Friday afternoon the dance hall that was called Roseland had a — you know it was a big dance hall — that’s where the musicians would come and look for gigs. And at that time all the Latin bands had trumpet players. And when you walked in the entrance the jazz musicians used to hang out on the left side, the Latin musicians hung out on the right side, and the vast majority of the club

date musicians hung out on the main dance floor. And every now and then someone from the Latin section needed a trumpet player so the word would filter over to the jazz section, where I used to hang out, and I got plenty of gigs that way, also developed a reputation because I was able to sight read very well and I could solo. So like I said, I got a lot of gigs that way.
What was the average price, the average bread that you might make on, I guess we could describe that as a pick-up gig?
In those days? $25. $30. Something like that.
And did you get that money in cash?
Okay. So you didn’t have to pay a union fee on that as long as you were paying your dues.

I wish, as a matter of fact, if all of the gigs that I played, including some with Mongo’s band and all the recordings that I did that I conducted afterwards, if all of that went to the union I would have a pension and a half. But most of them did not go through the union. But you know I was in it for the music and that’s what counted.
